rationale:
Evidence: iteration 3 is the best so far (score 335.3). Oval finished 9 of 20 runs (mean progress 0.94). S-bend (progress 0.61) and slalom (progress 0.31) still ended off track in every run. Iteration 3 cut max_error and line losses compared with iteration 2, and the ki increase from 0.02 to 0.3 coincided with the largest gain. That fits the idea that a constant left/right motor mismatch is being partly cancelled by the integral term. Steering oscillation rose on s-bend (0.37), which suggests the loop is still underdamped on tight alternating bends. Slalom progress is weakest, which points to slow response on rapid direction changes.

Changes: (1) ki 0.3 to 0.5, to push harder on the constant bias the integral is meant to cancel. The integral stays clamped at +/-2, so windup risk is bounded. (2) kd 0.5 to 0.6, to add damping against the higher oscillation seen on s-bend. (3) kp, base_speed, geometry and line_loss are unchanged, so the effect of the integral and derivative changes can be read on their own. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress rise, and max_error stays below 0.06 m on more runs. Oval completions should hold, and s-bend may gain its first completions. Hypotheses: (a) rms_error falls further as ki rises, which means the bias is still uncancelled; (b) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.4 on slalom, kd is adding noise rather than damping, and kd should come back down. Measurements wanted next: completion and completion_time per track, progress and max_error by track, rms_error and line_loss_events to judge ki, and steering_oscillation to judge kd.
